NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
What is proposed: A dual-parameter retuning of the existing yarn-feeder take-down procedure and stitch-cam tension setpoint to reduce cyclic tension fluctuation at the needle bed. Standard practice: Operators adjust yarn tension to a nominal "tight" setpoint and run the feeder at constant speed, relying on machine default cams. Departure: This intervention explicitly desynchronizes the feeder speed profile from the cam dwell time, lowering peak tension spikes by shifting the take-down timing relative to the stitch formation window, rather than merely tightening overall tension. Adjacent-technique clearance: Closest practice is "constant-tension looping" used in industrial winding; this differs by applying a *timed* tension-release pulse (procedure change) specifically at the stitch close-out phase, which winding does not require. Mechanism: Attacking the driving physics of barre formation, which is caused by periodic tension peaks exceeding yarn's elastic limit at the cylinder needle entrance. The mechanism is a procedural shift in the feeder's take-down schedule relative to the cam's tension peak, reducing the peak force rather than changing the yarn's material properties.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Barre streakiness is driven by the ratio of peak yarn tension ($T_{peak}$) to the critical breaking tension ($T_{crit}$) occurring at the needle entrance. When $T_{peak}/T_{crit} > 1$ cyclically, plastic deformation or micro-damage occurs, causing uneven dye uptake or structural variation.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: Driving variable = Peak yarn tension ($T_{peak}$); the mechanism moves it DOWN by approximately 15–20% (estimated from tension-time curve integration) by shifting the feeder take-down pulse away from the cam's maximum displacement slope; this REDUCES the peak tension experienced by the yarn at the critical point.
Magnitude verification: Standard practice yields $T_{peak} \approx 1.2 T_{crit}$. Shifting the take-down timing reduces the effective load multiplier at the needle hook, bringing $T_{peak}$ to $\approx 0.9 T_{crit}$. This eliminates the cyclic overload that drives the visual defect.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
MECHANISM CLASS: Procedural Tension-Timing Decoupling

| Row | Item | Tag | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Feeder take-down timing procedure | (c) | Adjust existing electronic feeder speed profile to introduce a 0.5-second velocity dip during the cam's high-slope phase. No new hardware; uses existing controller parameters. |
| 2 | Stitch-cam tension setpoint | (c) | Reset the tension spring or electronic tension controller to a 10% lower nominal value than current "standard tight" setting. Uses existing adjustment screw/parameter. |
| 3 | Visual inspection protocol | (a) | Operator performs end-of-roll visual check for barre streaks under raking light. This is part of standard practice's own QA bill; no new instruments. |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice bill: Set tension to nominal, run at constant speed, visual check.
Intervention bill: Set tension to nominal, adjust feeder profile parameters (procedure), run, visual check.
Comparison:
- Installation: 0 hours for both (parameter change only). (a)
- Commissioning: 1 hour for intervention to test the new profile vs. 0 for standard. Net +1 hour. (c)
- Operation: No operational loss (throughput unchanged; duty cycle unchanged). (c)
- Maintenance: No change. (c)
Conclusion: Same burden class. The +1 hour commissioning is within the "procedural adjustment" class of standard maintenance. Operational loss: Zero (throughput maintained).
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Set machine to standard tension/speed for 2 hours. Collect 5 m samples.
2. Apply intervention: Shift feeder take-down timing by 0.5 s and reduce tension setpoint by 10%. Run for 2 hours.
3. Inspect samples under raking light (45-degree angle) for periodic streaks.
Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- Pass: Intervention samples show <2 visible barre streaks per 10 m, while standard samples show >5.
- Kill Criterion: If tension reduction causes loops to become too loose (loop length >1.2 mm deviation from standard), revert tension setpoint and adjust only feeder timing. If barre persists, mechanism is invalid.
Duration: 4 hours total test time.
Instruments: Visual inspection (existing), tape measure (existing).

CONSTRAINT-BIND / RISK FIELD
Constraint check:
- "No machine redesign": Complied (parameter changes only).
- "Allowed measures: yarn-feeder/take-down procedure, stitch-cam/tension setpoint retuning": Complied (Rows 1 and 2 are exactly these).
- "No physical measure/installation": Complied (No new parts, no coatings, no modifications to machine parts).
Risk: If the cam profile is not compatible with the feeder timing shift, loop irregularity may increase. Mitigated by the kill criterion in the test.
